attribution.note: Marcus directly asserts the enterprise observation in his own voice.

semantics.note: The proposition preserves the substantial-group scope and mild disappointment. ChatGPT is implied by context; the schoolchildren statement is separable.

contract.note: The plain reading reasonably requires a substantial disappointed group, without demanding a majority or denying useful results. Its population, product and experience requirements are fair.

evidence.note: Contemporaneous reporting documents one unnamed customer's dissatisfaction with Copilot, but establishes neither Fortune 500 membership nor prevalence. Microsoft's favorable accounts are company disclosures.
Valid contemporary survey context, but broad AI value findings do not identify Fortune 500 ChatGPT users or measure disappointment against expectations.
Relevant contemporary reporting includes favorable assessments and deployment difficulties. It does not isolate Fortune 500 firms; finding some value does not exclude disappointment.

reviews.rationale: The packet establishes neither a substantial disappointed group among Fortune 500 users of the relevant products nor that such disappointment was rare. Broader survey findings and an unnamed customer account cannot settle the observation. Favorable assessments also do not contradict its limited scope.
